skills.name: Solve quadratic equations with the quadratic formula

note.text:
For ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0), the solutions are x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a.
• Write the equation with zero on one side and read a, b, c with their signs.
• Work out the discriminant D = b² − 4ac first.
• D > 0: two different roots; D = 0: one repeated root; D < 0: no real roots.
• The formula works even when the quadratic does not factorise; give roots to the accuracy asked (often 2 decimal places).

sections.heading: When factorising fails
sections.text:
Some quadratics, such as {poly([1, 'x²'], [3, 'x'], [-1, ''])} = {0}, have no whole-number factors. The quadratic formula always works:
x = (−b ± √(b² − {4}ac)) ÷ {2}a
Here a is the coefficient of x², b of x, and c is the number term, each read with its sign after making one side zero.
The ± means: do it once with + and once with −. That gives the two roots.

sections.heading: What the discriminant tells you
sections.text:
D = b² − {4}ac is under the square root.
• D positive: two different real roots.
• D zero: √{0} = {0}, so both roots are the same (one repeated root).
• D negative: there is no real square root, so no real roots.
Check D first: it tells you what to expect before you finish the calculation.

key_words.meaning: D = b² − {4}ac, the part under the square root

mistake.why: The formula starts with −b. Here b = {-5}, so −b = {5}.

worked_example.problem: Solve {poly([a, 'x²'], [b, 'x'], [c, ''])} = {0}, giving the roots to {2} decimal places.
steps: x ≈ {roundTo((-b + sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)} or x ≈ {roundTo((-b - sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)}.
worked_example.answer: x ≈ {roundTo((-b + sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)} or x ≈ {roundTo((-b - sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)}

cards.idea: Read a, b and c with their signs from ax² + bx + c = {0}.
Work out the discriminant D = b² − {4}ac first.
The sign of D tells you how many real roots there are.
example: D = {13} > {0}: two roots.  D = {0}: one root.  D = {-7}: none.

check.prompt: How many real roots does {poly([a, 'x²'], [b, 'x'], [c, ''])} = {0} have?
check.correct: {b * b - 4 * a * c > 0 ? 'Two different roots' : b * b - 4 * a * c == 0 ? 'One repeated root' : 'No real roots'}

distractors.text: {b * b - 4 * a * c > 0 ? 'One repeated root' : 'Two different roots'}
{b * b - 4 * a * c < 0 ? 'One repeated root' : 'No real roots'}
{'It depends on the value of x'}

misconceptions.explain: Use D = b² − {4}ac = {b * b - 4 * a * c}: positive gives two roots, zero one, negative none.
Use D = b² − {4}ac = {b * b - 4 * a * c}: positive gives two roots, zero one, negative none.
The number of roots is fixed by a, b and c through D = b² − {4}ac, not by x.

misconceptions.explain: Keep the signs: b = {b} and c = {c} are negative.
a goes with x², c is the number term.
b goes with x and c is the number term.

solution: a is the coefficient of x², b of x, and c is the number term, each with its sign.

questions.prompt: Work out the discriminant b² − 4ac for {poly([a, 'x²'], [b, 'x'], [c, ''])} = {0}.

misconceptions.explain: Keep the sign of c: {4} × {a} × {br(c)} = {4 * a * c}.

where: b * b - 4 * a * c != b * b + 4 * a * c

questions.prompt: Solve {poly([a, 'x²'], [b, 'x'], [c, ''])} = {0} with the formula. Give the larger root to {2} decimal places.
questions.answer: roundTo((-b + sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)

misconceptions.explain: Divide the whole top by {2 * a}.

misconceptions.wrong: roundTo((b + sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)

where: roundTo(-b + sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c), 0.01) != roundTo((-b + sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)

questions.prompt: Solve {poly([a, 'x²'], [b, 'x'], [c, ''])} = {0} with the formula. Give the smaller root to {2} decimal places.
questions.answer: roundTo((-b - sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)

misconceptions.wrong: roundTo((-b + sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c)) / (2 * a), 0.01)
misconceptions.explain: That is the larger root (with +). The smaller one uses −√D.

solution: D = {b * b - 4 * a * c}, √D ≈ {roundTo(sqrt(b * b - 4 * a * c), 0.0001)}.
The smaller root uses minus: x = ({-b} − √{b * b - 4 * a * c}) ÷ {2 * a} ≈ {answer}.
